quickAnswer: Commercial office move-in and move-out cleaning costs $0.18 to $0.45 per square foot—or $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour—with strict $180 to $350 one-time mobilization minimums. For a 5,000 sq ft office with two restrooms, a light move-in pre-occupancy sanitization runs $900 to $1,450, whereas a full move-out deep turnover with appliance cleanouts, interior glass, and floor restoration runs $1,500 to $2,250.

blocks.text: Office managers frequently experience sticker shock when requesting a one-time turnover quote from their regular janitorial contractor. If recurring 3x/week service runs **$0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft** on a 5,000 sq ft suite, why does vacating or occupying that exact same floor plate cost **$0.18 to $0.45 per sq ft**?

The answer lies in scope density and one-time mobilization overhead. Routine maintenance built into our [office cleaning cost guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) wipes open work surfaces and empties bins at roughly **3,500 sq ft per labor hour**, whereas an empty-suite turnover exposes years of baseboard dust, cubicle-wall shadow lines, ceiling vent soot, cabinet interiors, and sticky cable-grommet residue that cut technician speed to **1,200 to 2,000 sq ft per hour**.
Move-In Sanitization vs. Move-Out Deep Turnover Pricing

Move-in and move-out quotes look identical on casual RFPs, yet their labor assumptions differ sharply. A **move-in clean** typically follows landlord build-out or previous tenant surrender and focuses on high-touch sanitization, HVAC diffuser wiping, restroom fixture descaling, and breakroom cabinet prep before IT teams unbox monitors. A **move-out clean**, by contrast, carries heavier soil removal, adhesive sticker scraping, refrigerator defrosting, and wall-scuff erasure—often governed by strict [broom-swept vs. white-glove lease clauses](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/lease-end-broom-swept-commercial-cleaning-cost/).

blocks.title: Why Recurring Contractors Discount Move-In Cleans
blocks.text: When you award a 12-month recurring contract alongside your move-in clean, commercial vendors frequently waive the $180 to $350 one-time dispatch premium or credit 25% to 50% of the initial deep-clean fee against your first full month of scheduled service.
Scope Line Items That Inflate Turnover Invoices

One-time turnover bids diverge most widely on specialty restoration tasks that fall outside base janitorial checklists. Restrooms require extra descaling (**$25 to $50 per restroom** compared to **$15 to $30** on recurring visits), breakroom appliances need full interior defrosting and degreasing (**$25 to $60 per kitchenette** vs. **$12 to $25** routine wipe-downs), and floor-to-ceiling conference glass often carries smeared tape marks (**$25 to $75** per boardroom).

blocks.text: Equipment Standards for Dust-Free Empty-Suite Turnovers

Vacant suites act like echo chambers for fine particulate dust—especially after movers unbolt modular workstations or contractors patch drywall anchors. Low-filtration vacuums blow pulverized gypsum and carpet fiber straight back onto freshly wiped ledges, forcing double dusting passes. Staging dedicated commercial tools from a [commercial janitorial cart](/janitorial-carts-mops-and-tools/best-commercial-janitorial-cleaning-carts/) prevents rework.

items: **Multi-Stage Particulate Capture:** The **Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro Backpack Vacuum** (6 qt capacity, 5-Stage HEPA filtration, 11 lb weight, 62 dBA rating) traps ultrafine drywall and baseboard dust along empty perimeter outlets without exhausting haze onto glass partitions.

**Heavy-Soil Corridor & Restroom Rinsing:** The **Rubbermaid Commercial WaveBrake 35-Quart Mop Bucket & Side-Press Wringer** (35 qt capacity, WaveBrake baffling, Side-Press wringer, 5-Yr Wringer rating) handles aggressive multi-pass rinsing across dusty VCT corridors and breakroom tile without sloshing baseboards.

**Cross-Contamination-Free Sanitization:** The **Rubbermaid Commercial HYGEN Charging Bucket** (20 pads capacity, Snap Lid, Color-Coded protocol, OSHA Ready) pre-saturates separate red microfiber pads for restroom stalls and blue/green pads for kitchenette counters so incoming employees step into genuinely hygienic surfaces.

blocks.title: Do Not Confuse Move-In Cleaning With Post-Construction Cleanup
blocks.text: If your new office underwent active tenant improvements—drywall sanding, ceiling grid cutting, or paint overspray—standard move-in rates ($0.18–$0.28/sq ft) will not cover the labor. Post-construction fine-dust cleaning requires three full HEPA passes and runs $0.35 to $0.75 per sq ft.
How Move-In Timing and Crew Size Affect Labor Rates

One-time turnovers rarely run with a solo custodian. A 5,000 sq ft move-out clean requiring **14 to 25 total labor hours** is typically staffed by a three- to four-person specialty crew over a single 6-hour evening or weekend window, ensuring floors dry cleanly before Monday occupancy or landlord inspection. Compressed weekend or same-day turnarounds add overtime labor inside the **$55 to $95 per specialty hour** band, whereas giving a vendor a flexible 72-hour window lets them dispatch standard **$35 to $65/hour** technicians.
Step-by-Step Checklist Before Scheduling Turnover Crews

Sequencing cleaning crews before furniture removal—or before IT cabling teams finish pulling Cat6 drops—guarantees you will pay twice. Align facility, IT, and building-management schedules using these five procurement checkpoints.

items.name: Confirm Empty Floor Plate & Trash Haul-Off
items.text: Require movers and IT teams to remove all pallets, broken chairs, and e-waste beforehand; janitorial crews charge $55 to $95/hr plus dumpster fees to haul abandoned furniture.

items.name: Secure Freight Elevator & Dock COI Endorsements
items.text: Submit your cleaner's Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M GL, Workers' Comp, Additional Insured naming the landlord) 72 hours prior to reserve after-hours freight elevator access.

items.name: Verify Active Power, HVAC, and Hot Water
items.text: Confirm electricity and hot water remain turned on during move-out turnovers so backpack vacuums, carpet extractors, and degreasing chemicals operate properly.

items.name: Separate Consumables From One-Time Turnovers
items.text: State clearly whether the vendor is stocking new paper towels, toilet tissue, and soap ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft equivalent) for move-in day or leaving dispensers empty on move-out.

items.name: Conduct a Final Blue-Tape Walk-Through
items.text: Walk the suite with the janitorial supervisor and property manager before crew sign-off so missed sticker adhesive or restroom grout spots are corrected before mobilization ends.

faqs.q: What insurance documentation do building managers require for one-time office turnovers?
faqs.a: Even for a single-day move-in or move-out job, Class A and Class B property managers require a Certificate of Insurance (COI) showing $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability, statutory Workers' Compensation, and Additional Insured wording naming both the tenant entity and building ownership.

faqs.q: How do OSHA HazCom and Bloodborne Pathogens rules apply to move-out cleanings?
faqs.a: Under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200), crews bringing adhesive removers, acid restroom descalers, or carpet spotters onsite must carry accessible Safety Data Sheets (SDS). If abandoned breakrooms or restrooms contain bodily fluids or spoiled bio-waste, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) PPE and $55 to $95/hr specialty rates apply.

faqs.q: Can move-in sanitization use Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice products?
faqs.a: Yes. Most corporate tenants request Green Seal GS-37 low-VOC cleaners and EPA Safer Choice disinfectants for move-in turnovers so new staff do not experience lingering fragrance or solvent odors on day one. Green chemistry typically adds 0% to 4% when paired with microfiber dilution systems.

faqs.q: What is usually excluded from a commercial move-out cleaning quote?
faqs.a: Standard move-out quotes exclude hauling broken cubicles or e-waste, patching drywall holes, painting, replacing stained ceiling tiles, server-room raised-floor sub-plenum cleaning, and exterior window washing above ground level unless explicitly quoted.

faqs.q: Why can't my cleaner bill a move-out clean at my regular 4.333-week contract rate?
faqs.a: Recurring contracts divide annual maintenance across 4.333 weeks per month (13.0 or 21.65 visits monthly) assuming light surface dusting and high production speeds of 3,500 sq ft/hr. One-time turnovers involve deep cabinet, baseboard, and fixture restoration at 1,200 to 2,000 sq ft/hr with zero recurring margin.
